To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the inhomogeneous and the intrinsic damping processes contribute to the damping of the giant dipol resonance; (2) the width of the giant resonance is larger than that expected from the thermal shape fluctuaton model; and (3) the width is well described by a simple empirical model.

the width of the giant resonance in hot nuclei shows a discrepancy with the prediction from a thermal shape fluctuation calculation, and that a new empirical form, describing both the temperature and angular-momentum dependence of the width of the resonance, should be used.
the width of the GDR shows a strong dependence on the angular momentum and that both the inhomogeneity and intrinsic damping processes should be considered in order to explain the observed behavior.

the study of giant dipole resonances (GDR) in hot rotating nuclei.

the inhomogeneous and intrinsic collisional damping mechanisms are equally important for the damping of the giant dipol resonance in hot rotating systems.
the inhomogeneous process dominates at low angular momenta and the intrinsic collision plays a more important role as angular momentum increases.
